bullets.text: Automated the weekly sales report across 38 stores, turning about six hours of manual spreadsheet work into a ten-minute scheduled job.
Found that 14% of SKUs caused 60% of stockouts, and the category team changed reorder levels for those items based on the analysis.
Built a Power BI dashboard of sales, margin and stock cover that five regional managers used in their weekly reviews.
Cleaned 2.1 million point-of-sale rows, resolving duplicate bills and store-code mismatches that had inflated reported sales in two regions.
Predicted which telecom customers will leave next month on a public 7,043-customer dataset, so retention offers reach the right people first.
Tuned an XGBoost classifier to ROC-AUC 0.86 against 0.79 for a logistic regression baseline, using stratified five-fold cross-validation.
Explained every prediction with SHAP values, showing a non-technical reader which contract and billing factors drove each customer's risk.
Chose the decision threshold from a cost model of retention offers rather than the default 0.5, trading recall against offer spend.
Forecast district-level rice yield from 20 years of public agriculture and rainfall records, for planning procurement before the harvest arrives.
Added rainfall regressors to Prophet, lowering MAPE from 18% to 11% against a seasonal naive baseline across the test seasons.
Evaluated with rolling-origin backtesting so no future season ever leaks into training, the mistake a random train-test split would make.
Mapped forecasts and their error bands per district with GeoPandas, making the weakest-forecast regions visible at a glance.

bullets.text: Classified sentiment in Tamil-English code-mixed product reviews, which English-only sentiment models misread because they ignore the Tamil half.
Fine-tuned multilingual BERT to macro-F1 0.78 against 0.64 for a TF-IDF logistic regression baseline on a held-out review set.
Hand-labelled 3,000 reviews with a second annotator, measuring agreement at Cohen's kappa 0.71 before training on the labels.
Served the model through a FastAPI endpoint at about 40 ms per review on CPU, with batched inference for bulk scoring.
Built an explorer over 90,000 public civic complaints so residents can see which kinds of complaints actually get resolved in their ward.
Computed median resolution time by ward and complaint type, surfacing drainage complaints as the slowest category in most wards.
Indexed the PostgreSQL tables behind each filter so every view responds in under a second on the full complaint history.
